title: Nidhara – Security-First Auth Foundation for a Personal Finance & Growth Platform
subtitle: NestJS, Prisma, and Next.js monorepo with Argon2 authentication, rotating refresh-token sessions, and audit logging.
description: Accomplished a hardened authentication foundation for a personal wealth and growth platform as measured by 5 REST endpoints, 6 Prisma models, 2 database migrations, and 30 documentation pages, by building Argon2 hashing, single-use rotating refresh tokens with CSRF checks, and structured Pino logging in a NestJS monorepo.

contribution.label: Solo owner & full-stack engineer
contribution.headline: Designed and built the monorepo, authentication engine, session lifecycle, Prisma data model, and documentation site alone.
scope: npm workspaces monorepo: NestJS backend, Next.js frontend, Docusaurus docs
Signup, signin, refresh, and logout flows with Argon2 and dual-token issuance
Database-backed sessions with CSRF verification and revocation on replay or logout
Security event, account security state, and sudo session data models
Swagger documentation, response envelope interceptor, and structured Pino logging

problem.statement: Personal finance and journaling tools are fragmented, and many leave users with weak credential storage and fragile session handling. A financial platform needs an auditable authentication foundation, with strict session invalidation, CSRF defenses, and event logging, in place before any ledgers are connected.

benefitMatrix.pain: Stolen or replayed session tokens could expose personal financial data
benefitMatrix.before: Long-lived refresh tokens in cookies with no replay detection
benefitMatrix.after: Single-use refresh tokens bound to a session record, rotated on every refresh and paired with a CSRF token

benefitMatrix.pain: No audit trail of sign-in activity
benefitMatrix.before: Unstructured console logs and no record of login outcomes
benefitMatrix.after: Security events (login success, login failure, logout, refresh rotation) stored with user-agent and IP metadata, plus structured JSON request logs

product.summary: Delivered the security foundation of a personal wealth and growth platform: Argon2 credentials, rotating refresh-token sessions with CSRF checks, audit events, and a documented monorepo ready for the finance ledger to be added.
product.problem: Financial tools need strong credential storage, strict session invalidation, and an audit trail before they handle money. Many personal apps add these late, or not at all.
product.tagline: Get authentication right before the ledger arrives.

valueProposition.targetCustomer: Individuals managing personal finances and life records

items.painDescription: Passwords hashed with older schemes are easier to attack with GPU-accelerated brute force.
items.gainDescription: Argon2 protects both passwords and stored refresh token hashes.

items.painDescription: Long-lived refresh tokens in cookies can be stolen or abused through cross-site requests.
items.gainDescription: Each refresh issues a new token, validates a matching CSRF token, and revokes the session on replay.

items.painDescription: Console logs are hard to search and do not record who tried to sign in or from where.
items.gainDescription: Login, logout, and refresh events are stored with IP and user-agent, and requests are logged as structured JSON.

keyDecisions.challenge: Protect credentials and session secrets against GPU-accelerated brute-force attacks.
keyDecisions.decision: Used Argon2 for credential verification and refresh token hashes instead of bcrypt. Trade-off: higher memory use per authentication request.
keyDecisions.outcome: Stronger resistance to hardware-assisted brute force on stored secrets.

keyDecisions.challenge: Long-lived refresh tokens in cookies risk theft and cross-site request forgery.
keyDecisions.decision: Bound each refresh token to a session record, rotated the refresh hash on every /auth/refresh call, and required a matching client csrfToken. Trade-off: extra database writes on refresh.
keyDecisions.outcome: Refresh token reuse is rejected and background refresh from another site is blocked.

keyDecisions.challenge: Sensitive account changes need re-authentication without interrupting the ongoing session.
keyDecisions.decision: Modeled a standalone SudoSession with a time-bounded sudoUntil and a verified escalation method (PASSWORD, RECOVERY_KEY, MFA). Trade-off: sensitive endpoints will need a second authorization check.
keyDecisions.outcome: A data model for step-up authentication is in place for when sensitive endpoints are built.

keyDecisions.challenge: Plain console logs are hard to search and weak as an audit trail.
keyDecisions.decision: Integrated nestjs-pino with pino-http and a global ResponseInterceptor to emit structured JSON logs and a uniform response envelope. Trade-off: some extra bootstrap configuration.
keyDecisions.outcome: Searchable request and response logs for auditing and debugging.

securityReliability: Argon2 hashing for passwords and refresh token hashes
Dual-token flow: short-lived access token plus httpOnly refresh cookie
Single-use refresh rotation with CSRF token verification; session revoked on replay or logout
Security events (LOGIN_SUCCESS, LOGIN_FAILED, LOGOUT, REFRESH_ROTATED) stored with IP and user-agent
Failed-login tracking and sudo session state modeled in the database
futureRoadmap: Financial accounts, immutable transaction ledgers, and savings goals
Personal development suite (LifeLog, Capsule, Knowledge base, Micro Actions)
